payload.goal: Widen collision detection past the initiative boundary without paying O(total history) on the hook path: two sessions on DIFFERENT initiatives editing one file are invisible today (the hook folds one slug; doctor loops slugs but detects per-slug). Gate the hot path on a git-proof warm-log signal — the true last-append time read from each log's TAIL, never mtime — and leave sofar doctor ungated so the exhaustive answer always exists. Measured budget: shim is 63-67ms of speed T2's 100ms; fold-all-30 costs +15.8ms and is O(history), gated costs ~+1.7ms and is O(concurrent activity).

payload.because: mtime is not append-only: `git checkout` rewrites every events.jsonl and makes all 30 look warm, collapsing the gate back to the +15.8ms all-fold path — the one measured failure mode. A tail read answers the same question from CONTENT rather than metadata, so a checkout, a copy, a restore, or a touch cannot move it. It is also O(1) per log regardless of file size, where mtime's cheapness came with the lie. An open-sessions index was rejected twice over: a repo-level one is not union-mergeable the way events.jsonl is (team-readiness T2) and would conflict on every parallel append, and a committed per-initiative marker would be restored stale by the same checkout, turning a cost blip into a MISSED warning. Doctor stays ungated because it is an on-demand audit, not on the 100ms critical path — so the exhaustive answer always remains available and the gate never loses information, it only narrows what is computed per keystroke.
payload.chose: Gate the hot path on the log's TRUE last-append time, read from the tail of events.jsonl (seek to end, take the newest ts among the last complete lines) — never on filesystem mtime. Keep sofar doctor ungated and exhaustive.
payload.over: the mtime gate the measurement used, folding every initiative on every prompt, and a maintained open-sessions index file
payload.rule: Never gate a hot-path scan on filesystem mtime — git rewrites it. Derive warmth from log content (the tail's newest ts), and keep sofar doctor ungated so the exhaustive answer always exists.

payload.text:
SCALE MEASURED 2026-08-08 — the warm gate fixes FOLD cost but not SCAN cost, and the scan is what binds at scale. Synthetic records, 200 events per initiative, 3 warm, median of 10:

  30 initiatives:   warm scan 2.0ms | gated total 2.4ms | ungated 4.7ms
  300 initiatives:  warm scan 18.9ms | gated total 19.0ms | ungated 47.2ms
  1000 initiatives: warm scan 64.1ms | gated total 66.4ms | ungated 176.6ms

At 300 the folding is FREE (19.0 total vs 18.9 scan) — every millisecond is the tail-read sweep itself. At 1000 the sweep alone (64ms) plus the shim's own 63-67ms is roughly double the speed T2 100ms budget. So warm-gating converts O(total history) into O(initiative count), which is better but still linear in the wrong variable.

This collides with an ALREADY-SETTLED law. core/graph.ts, the repo's only other cross-record derivation, states: "Never in the hot path — this reads N logs where a shim can afford one (speed T2); its only consumers are explicit CLI surfaces and doctor." Any cross-record scan on UserPromptSubmit is a deviation from that and needs its own decision.

Three ways forward, unresolved:
(a) Ship the hook gated AND capped by initiative count (~200 keeps it inside budget). Works for essentially every real repo today, but the feature silently vanishes for the largest users — the worst failure shape.
(b) Honour graph.ts's law: cross-initiative conflicts live in `sofar doctor` only, ungated and exhaustive, and never touch the shim. Zero budget risk, zero deviation; the warning arrives when audited rather than when it matters.
(c) INDEX IT. A repo-level append-only `.sofar/sessions.jsonl` carrying only session lifecycle (slug, session id, started/ended, ts). Session events are rare, so the file stays tiny; a tail read answers "which initiatives hold OPEN sessions" in O(1) regardless of initiative count — exact, not heuristic, and strictly better than warmth. Append-only means it takes the same `merge=union` treatment as events.jsonl (team-readiness T2). Truth stays in the per-initiative logs; this is a derived index, so absent/corrupt falls back to the full scan and correctness is preserved. Costs: a new artifact in SPEC §layout, a rebuild path, and write amplification on session lifecycle only.

(c) is the real answer and the only one that keeps the gains at Gmail scale. It is also a record-layout change, so it is the user's call, not mine.

NOT a problem, and worth stating because it is the natural worry: none of this touches the model's orientation context. renderStatus folds the ONE bound initiative, so goal, decisions, standing constraints and rejected approaches cost the same at 1000 initiatives as at 3. Reasoning context does not degrade with record size; only cross-record SCANS do.

payload.note: core/warmth.ts + 9 tests green. The headline pin is git-checkout immunity: utimes the file to now, content unchanged, still reads cold — the mtime gate would have called it warm. Also pinned: newest-ts not last-line (backdated appends), partial first line dropped, whole-file fallback when one event exceeds the tail window, corrupt lines skipped as the fold skips them, and unreadable counts as WARM so ambiguity costs a fold rather than a dropped warning.

core/cross-conflicts.ts: warm-gated when given a window, exhaustive without one — the single derivation both the hook and doctor can use. Extracted openSessionFiles() in core/fold.ts so liveness (the alsoLiveSessionId re-admission, the +N sentinel skip) has ONE definition rather than drifting copies. initiativeSlugs moved to core/listing with a re-export from mcp/context so core never reaches up into mcp. Full suite green (1132).

Blocked on the scale ruling (see the scale note). Wiring a cross-record scan into UserPromptSubmit deviates from core/graph.ts's standing law that cross-record derivations never touch the hot path, and the measurement shows why: the scan is O(initiative count) — 18.9ms at 300, 64ms at 1000 against a 100ms budget the shim already spends 63-67ms of. Needs the user to pick (a) gated+capped hook, (b) doctor-only, or (c) the session-lifecycle index that makes it O(1). Do not wire the hook before that choice.

doctor's Concurrency axis now reports both scopes, the cross one ungated and computed from states it had already folded (zero extra I/O). Verified live against this repo through the built engine. This is the half that is correct under every option in the scale ruling, which is why it landed ahead of it.

SPEC covers what shipped: doctor's two-scope concurrency axis, plus acceptance blocks for the warm-log signal (git-checkout immunity, newest-not-last, partial-line, whole-file fallback, warm-on-ambiguity) and cross-initiative concurrency (no double-reporting, re-admission across the boundary, gate changes what is READ never what counts). The hook wording waits on 2.2's ruling.

payload.next_action: Rule on 2.2: (a) gated+capped hook, (b) doctor-only per graph.ts's law, or (c) append-only .sofar/sessions.jsonl lifecycle index making the hook O(1) at any scale — (c) recommended.
payload.summary: Built the gate correctly and found its real limit. core/warmth.ts derives warmth from the log's TAIL, not mtime, so git checkout can no longer fake it (pinned). core/cross-conflicts.ts is the one derivation for both scopes; openSessionFiles extracted so liveness has a single definition. doctor now reports cross-initiative conflicts ungated, verified live. SPEC + 18 new tests, 1141 green. BUT the scale probe shows warm-gating converts O(history) into O(initiative count): scan alone is 18.9ms at 300 initiatives and 64ms at 1000, against a shim already spending 63-67ms of 100ms. Hook wiring (2.2) left BLOCKED on that ruling.
